summary: BA cycle 3 ticket has 4 blocking defects. (1) Decision 2 grants Write/Edit/MultiEdit to timeline/transportation in policy, contradicting the agents' own declared `tools:` list AND re-enabling the documented Feb-13-2026 incident bug class (Write corrupted timeline.json, 20 days lost). (2) Decision 1 shape-based dispatch creates an internal AC inconsistency: AC12 demands blocking a path-shaped string inside Edit.old_string, AC15 demands NOT blocking a documentation reference to the same path; the 'realpath under denied prefix' heuristic cannot satisfy both. (3) AC9 'all 6 surfaces exit 0' cannot be tested because the proposed roles do not grant WebFetch/MCP tool surfaces — the standard allowed_tools check will deny them BEFORE any gaode pre-check fires. (4) AC15 uses `subagent_type:"meals"` but `meals` is NOT in `roles{}` (cycle 3 only adds timeline+transportation); the hook returns 'unknown role meals' → exit 2; AC15 as written cannot exit 0. Plus 5 additional findings (3 major, 2 minor). Codex unanimously confirms findings (1) (2) and surfaces (4) independently. BA must revise ticket cycle 3 before /redev → dev.

objections.claim_under_review: Shape-based dispatch (path-shaped → read-path matcher; free-text → NOT scanned) prevents the documentation false-positive (Decision 1 + AC12 + AC15)
evidence_against: AC12 (ticket lines 445-450) requires that `Edit.old_string:"path = '/root/.claude/skills/gaode-maps/skill.md'"` (a path-shaped substring inside an old_string) → exit 2 with surface:read-path
AC15 (ticket line 467) requires that `Grep.pattern:"gaode-maps"` from meals → exit 0 (free text in pattern field NOT scanned)

AC12 and Decision 1 are internally inconsistent: if the scanner extracts path-shaped substrings from ANY string leaf (so it can catch the case in AC12), then a documentation Edit on the ticket file containing the literal path `'see /root/.claude/skills/gaode-maps/skill.md'` will ALSO match (because the same substring extraction fires). The 'free-text NOT scanned' rule cannot distinguish 'a path-quoted string in a Python source file being edited' from 'a path mentioned in prose documentation being edited' — both look identical at the substring level

Codex confirmed: 'either scanner treats the whole leaf as one path → AC12 will not actually block; or scanner extracts embedded path substrings → documentation edits containing that path will be blocked'
objections.impact: Decision 1's shape-based dispatch is BA's MOST consequential architectural choice and BA's own primary defense against the documentation-blackhole regression. As specified, the heuristic cannot satisfy AC12 and AC15 simultaneously. Whichever way dev implements it, one of the two ACs will fail. The 永久彻底修复 directive will not be met.

This makes the scanner's 'where' explicit and matches what fields actually carry path-typed data in the tool schemas
